# Miami, round three

Round two is merged and is now the example to beat. Read `BRIEF.md`, `BRIEF_ROUND2.md`, `REPORT.md`, `STATE.md`, `style/STYLE.md` and `tools/mapart/README.md`, and look at the tiles of every zoom before anything else.

## What round two got right, and must keep

- The far zooms are drawn for their scale: districts as masses, a handful of landmarks as small pictures, the port with its sheds and cranes, the paper showing through the washes.
- The story reads at first glance on land: skeletal towers, drowned ground, broken spans.
- Zoom 3 is rich, and its water is painted: brush strokes, wave marks, pale shallows that follow the land.
- Measured apart from your own audit: no seam (worst join 1.24 times the jump beside it, over all 140 joins), each zoom against the one above within 1.6 to 2.8 of 255 in broad colour, painted water on the base water at 0.97.
- The rule from your coordinates to the engine's, in `base/VALUES.md`.

## Why there is a round three

The owner's rule has not changed: work short of the bar is done again, with no limit on time or cost, and the bar is a map someone would frame. Three things are short, as seen by someone looking at the pictures.

1. **The far water is not painted.** At zooms 0, 1 and 2 the bay is one flat teal with a soft glow along every shore. More than half of the whole-map picture is water, so more than half of the picture is blank. Your own zoom 3 shows you can paint water. A far zoom should not shrink those strokes; it should chart the bay for its scale, as an explorer would: where it is shallow and where a ship can pass. The real bay has that story (flats and shoals, the dredged cut to the port and its turning basin, the waterway, bars off the beach, the reef line off the ocean shore), and the drowned city adds its own: sunken spans, wrecks, the shoreline that was. No depth data was acquired in the earlier rounds. Public soundings and coastal elevation models exist; if you use one, record its source and licence as you did for the others, and say in the report where depth is drawn from data and where it is invented. The glow at the shore reads as a compositing halo, not as shallows.
   The game draws coloured cells and markers over the map, on water too, so the water must stay calm enough for a marker to read. Calm is not blank.
2. **The small marks repeat.** Your report says it: palms and courtyard ruins share one vocabulary, and at zooms 0 and 1 the landmark pictures are nearly one drawing several times. A survivor finds their way by what is different: give places their own pictures and their own small stories, so that two people can tell each other where they are by describing what is drawn there. Still no lettering.
3. **The mainland's bay shore at zooms 0 and 1** is a stepped, ruled edge with a dashed line. A quay is straight in life, but a hand draws a straight quay with a living line.

## What to do

Paint again where it falls short, with a free hand as before, and leave alone what is at the bar. Decide by looking. Before you call it finished, put the new whole-map zoom beside round two's (git history keeps it; reading history is fine) and ask whether the water half of the picture is now worth looking at, and whether a stranger could name five different places on it.

What must hold is unchanged: true to the data at each zoom for what that zoom draws, no seams, zooms that agree in broad colour, tiles of 1,024 pixels named as before, no lettering, border, compass or grid. Say plainly in the report where it still falls short.

## Practical

Replace tiles and originals in place and update `REPORT.md` and `STATE.md`. Keep what a reader needs to judge the work in `REPORT.md` or under `reports/`, not under `checks/`. Do not run git commands that write: the work is committed for you when the run ends. Network access is on. The virtual environment under `tools/mapart/.venv` is still there.

# Miami map-art tools

Offline source/art tools only. They add no dependency to the engine or its build.

## Current delivery: round two

The original geographic pipeline below remains authoritative for source layers. The current art finish is **round2.py**, followed by **round2_balance.py**. Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.

Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
```

Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. `round2_restore.py` reconstructs these for z2/z3 without altering the historical used prompts; run it immediately after `reference.py`, as above. Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals. The context-generation tools listed below are for commissioning new paintings and can overwrite prompts; they are not part of the reproduction sequence.

| Round-two tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.

The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

## Original geographic preparation and round-one tools

From the repository root, create the isolated environment:

```sh
python3 -m venv tools/mapart/.venv
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/pip install -r tools/mapart/requirements.txt
```

The frozen bounds, projection and sample conventions are in `assets/source/maps/miami/map.json`. Python 3.9 was used; exact package versions are pinned. Raw data and the virtual environment are ignored by git.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| fetch.py | Download intersecting NOAA DEM tiles, county TIGER ZIPs, NLCD coverage and paginated FEMA footprints. Write exact request URLs and SHA-256 checksums to downloads.json. Reuses existing downloads. |
| prepare.py | Clip/reproject vectors, reproject bare-earth height, rasterize 4,065 vertex samples, preserve NLCD codes, author explicit succession and low-street flooding. Checks FEMA pages against the complete object-ID inventory. |
| future.py | Freeze four missing bridge spans and four submerged wrecks as shared world geometry; mark tunnels as subterranean. Run after prepare.py. |
| reference.py [zooms...] | Render geographic references afresh from the vector data at each native zoom, with water/road/building masks. Default: all four zooms. |
| contexts.py Z | Build each tile's 64 px neighboring overlap, parent-paint context, exact prompt and queue.json for the built-in image tool. |
| finish.py Z | Similarity registration, local shoreline registration, class-constrained pigment and architectural detail, overlapping assembly, parent-color matching, exact cutting into 1,024 px PNGs. Requires every original painting for that zoom. |
| finish.py Z --partial | Pilot only: export already-painted tiles while keeping explicitly provisional parent proxies under checks/partial_zZ.png. Never use partial images as a completed delivery. |
| alignment.py | Position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC registration of original ink against geographic corners, with multistart main-water-silhouette similarity fitting for sparse scenes. Used by finish.py; cache metadata retains fit residuals and transforms. |
| preregister.py Z --watch | Populate registration caches as originals arrive. Stops when that zoom is complete; does not export tiles. |
| author_canopy.py | Freeze vegetation crowns from the complete registered zoom-3 painting as shared fictional world layers. Run once, then finish zooms 0 through 3 in order. |
| canonical.py | Save 8,192 px canonical water/road/building masks; repair classifications at inclusive outer grid samples and preserve surface roads over tunnels. Run after native references. |
| measure.py | Independently classify visible features from exported RGB; measure IoU, symmetric boundary distances, exact tile reconstruction, seam jumps, and parent-scale color differences. |
| grid_check.py | Quantify the difference between the engine's 2 m vertex samples and the finest native vector masks, independently of artwork. |
| review.py Z reference/raw/final [--row R] | Labeled contact sheets for review, under checks; never adds labels to game tiles. |
| audit.py | Assert tile count, RGB format, original-paint presence, base dimensions and bit depth; hash delivery artifacts. |

Build sources and references:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/fetch.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/prepare.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/future.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/canonical.py
```

Image generation is an explicit art-production step using the **built-in image tool**, not an API-key script. The overview prompt is under paintings/z0; later queues are made by contexts.py. Each queue entry lists its geometry reference, accepted parent, original style sheet and output filename. Inspect inputs, issue the prompt with those local references, then copy the returned original PNG to `paintings/zZ/C_R.raw.png`. Preserve supplementary prompt files. Do not resize or overwrite the raw originals. The tool returned 1,254 px squares during this run. The finishing code maps each to its 1,152 px overlap region (or 1,024 px overview).

After a complete zoom is painted:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/finish.py 1
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/contexts.py 2
```

Review the full map, representative full-resolution tiles, and joined boundaries. Exact geometry measurements do not establish artistic quality. Never accept solely on an RGB-mask score.

The offline viewer is `assets/source/maps/miami/checks/viewer.html`; open it directly in a browser. It reads the actual PNG tiles, supports pan/zoom and a fixed-camera painting comparison, and draws optional diagnostic overlays independently. No server or dependencies are required.

For final acceptance after every original exists, run `finish.py 3`, `author_canopy.py`, then `finish.py 0`, `finish.py 1`, `finish.py 2`, `finish.py 3`, `measure.py`, `grid_check.py` and `audit.py`. Preserve the frozen canopy during later finishing runs. `contexts.py` leaves prompts and reference crops for already-painted tiles intact. Exact fresh image generation is nondeterministic; the saved originals make subsequent finishing reproducible.

Do not change map.json after downloading and preparing an accepted map. To explore different bounds, use a separate destination and manifest: the download cache filenames describe this frozen square. See SOURCES.md and base/VALUES.md for source limits, licensing and authored-world conventions.

# A painted map of Miami

You are making the in-game world map for a survival game: the picture a player opens to see where they are. This is the first painted map the project has, and it is the example every later map will be held to. You have a free hand in how you do it. This brief says what it is for, what excellent looks like, what must hold, and what we learned from a first test. It is guidance, not a procedure.

## What it is for

The game is a survival game in the manner of ARK: Survival Evolved, with its own original art. Its maps will be ruined, overgrown cities built from public geographic data. The first is Miami.

The map screen shows a painted picture of the world with a coordinate grid over it (latitude and longitude from 0 to 100, as ARK has), player markers, and coloured cells where bases stand. The game draws the grid, the markers and the cells itself, over your picture. So the picture has to be true to the world: a coast on the map is a coast in the game.

The map has four zooms, baked in advance. Zoom 0 is the whole map in one tile. Each zoom doubles: 2 by 2 tiles, 4 by 4, and 8 by 8 at zoom 3. Every tile is a square picture, 1,024 pixels a side. Each zoom is its own picture drawn for its scale, not a shrunk copy of the one below.

## The example

A square of Miami about 8 km on a side, north up: downtown, the port, Biscayne Bay and its causeways, South Beach. The engine's ground grid is 2 m cells in chunks of 64 m, and the largest map it takes today is 127 chunks, 8,128 m, so make the square exactly that and say where its corners are.

It is Miami long after people: flooded streets, mangrove taking the shore back, towers standing as ruins, causeways broken, the beach wide and wild. Recognisably Miami in its coastline, street pattern and districts.

Painted in the manner of ARK's in-game maps, by description: aged parchment, confident ink linework, watercolour washes, shorelines with a darker ink edge and pale shallows, relief and built-up areas shown with hatching and small drawn symbols. A map an explorer drew. Describe the style to the image tool in words and build our own style sheet; do not give it other games' map pictures.

## The bar

A map someone would frame. Better than our test map, which is the example to beat: `planning/artist-test/map/map_1024.png` and its two double-zoom quarters, with the brief that made them in `planning/artist-test/briefs/map.md` and the report in `planning/artist-test/map/REPORT.md`.

- One hand across all four zooms: the same palette, line weight and symbols, so zooming feels like leaning closer to one drawing.
- Each zoom drawn for its scale. The far zoom broad and bold: the bay, the islands, the districts as shapes. The near zoom rich: individual ruined blocks, causeway spans, mangrove edges, sandbars, wrecks, the grid of streets.
- Detail that rewards looking, and no mush: nothing that reads as filler or noise.
- No lettering, no compass rose, no border and no grid lines in the tiles. The game draws its own grid and labels.

## What must hold

- **True to the data.** Every coast, island, road and built block is where the data puts it, to within a couple of pixels at each zoom.
- **No seams.** Tile joins to tile with nothing to see, across and down, at every zoom.
- **Zooms agree.** A zoom shrunk to the scale of the one above shows the same world in the same colours.

Measure these your own way and report the numbers. They will also be measured independently.

## The data

Public-domain and CC0 sources already identified for Miami:

- The 2021 Miami-Dade LiDAR hosted by NOAA (CC0), with points classified as ground, buildings, vegetation, water and bridges, and the bare-earth elevation raster made from it.
- USGS 3DEP elevation (public domain).
- Census TIGER roads (CC0 in the federal catalogue).
- FEMA USA Structures building outlines.
- USGS NLCD land cover.

Use only sources whose licence lets the result be redistributed freely, and record each one.

Make base layers on the map's own grid (4,065 samples a side at 2 m, or finer if it helps the painting): height, water, land cover, roads, building blocks. These same layers will later become the playable world through the engine's map file, so the painting and the world agree by construction. Keep them as plain files (16-bit PNG for height, 8-bit PNG for classes) with a note saying what each value means.

## What the first test taught

- Work out a style sheet and palette before the big pictures: how sea, shallows, beach, mangrove, swamp, ruin blocks, causeways, roads and height are each drawn. Then every picture is made against it and biomes stay consistent.
- The image tool returns pictures of about 1,254 pixels a side whatever is asked, which suits one tile per picture.
- The image tool alone does not hold a shoreline in place. In the test the painting was warped and composited against the water mask, which made it exact. That worked; better ideas are welcome.
- Give each zoom a reference rendered at that zoom's own resolution. In the test the double-zoom tiles followed an enlarged mask and their shores came out stepped.
- Painting a tile with its neighbours' edges and the zoom above as context kept the hand consistent and the seam invisible.
- Every accepted picture is a reference for the next.

## Where things go

Everything lives in the repository so another team can pick it up and see how it was made.

- `assets/source/maps/miami/`: this brief, `SOURCES.md` (each dataset: address, licence, date, checksum, what was taken), the base layers, the reference renders, the style sheet, every accepted picture, the finished tiles as `tiles/z<zoom>/<column>_<row>.png` with column 0 at the west and row 0 at the north, and `REPORT.md`.
- `assets/source/maps/miami/raw/`: downloads. Keep this folder out of git with a `.gitignore`, since the datasets are large and `SOURCES.md` says how to fetch them again.
- `tools/mapart/`: whatever tools you write, with a short `README.md` saying what each does and how to run it. Python is fine here. The engine and its build have no outside dependencies and that will not change, so keep any packages your tools need in a virtual environment inside `tools/mapart/` that git ignores, and list them with versions. No geodata libraries are installed on this machine; writing a small reader of your own for a format is welcome where practical.
- Touch nothing else in the repository. Do not run git commands that write: your work is committed for you when a run ends.

## How to work

- Work in stages and keep your state on disk: a short `STATE.md` saying what is done, what is accepted and what is next, so that a later run can carry on from it.
- Show something whole early. A good order is the style sheet, zoom 0, zoom 1, then one district carried all the way down to zoom 3, then the rest.
- Look at your pictures. Iterate until you would ship them.
- Several tiles can be worked at once if you can keep the hand consistent.
- Disk is plentiful (about 300 GB free). Network access is on for downloading the data.

## Report

Write `assets/source/maps/miami/REPORT.md` as you go: what you made and how, the sources, your measurements, what you are proud of, what falls short of the bar and why, and how long each stage took. End each run by saying plainly where things stand.
# Miami, round two

The first round is in this folder and is committed: 85 tiles in four zooms, the base layers, the style sheet, every original painting, the report. Read `BRIEF.md`, `REPORT.md`, `STATE.md`, `style/STYLE.md` and `tools/mapart/README.md`, and look at the tiles before anything else.

## What round one got right, and must keep

- It is true to the data. Coasts, roads and buildings sit where the layers put them.
- No seam shows. Measured independently across all 140 tile joins, the jump across a join is the jump beside it (worst 1.29 times).
- The zooms agree. Each zoom shrunk onto the one above differs by under 2 of 255 in broad colour.
- The nearest zoom has real richness: roofless blocks with rooms, palms and scrub through them, flooded streets, pale shallows.
- Everything is reproducible from the saved originals.

## Why there is a round two

The bar was "a map someone would frame". Round one is an accurate, handsome, tinted plan. It is not yet a drawn map, and the project's owner has asked that work short of the bar be done again, with no limit on time or cost: "aim for the stars". These are the reasons, as seen by someone looking at the pictures, not at the numbers.

1. **The far zooms are not drawn for their scale.** Zoom 0 shows every building and every street of the city at eight metres a pixel. It reads as a street plan seen from far away: a grey-and-tan mesh. An explorer drawing the whole bay would not draw eleven thousand buildings. They would draw the districts as masses with their own character, a handful of landmarks as small pictures (a cluster of ruined towers, the port's sheds and cranes, the broken bridges), bold coasts, and the water. Round one's own report says this: "the exact city fabric is denser at zoom 0 than a freely generalized explorer's atlas would be". At the far zooms, be true to the coast, the islands, the causeways and the main roads, and generalise the rest. The game draws coloured cells for players' bases and markers over the map, so the far zooms need room to breathe.
2. **The shore is a ruled line.** Every coast and island edge is a razor-straight vector edge with one dark line of one weight. It looks like survey output laid under a painting. A drawn coast has a line that thickens and thins, wavers a little, breaks at a beach and doubles at a quay, with shallows that follow it. "Within a couple of pixels" leaves room for a hand.
3. **The story is faint.** This is Miami long after people. At the far zooms the causeways look intact, the streets look dry and the city looks inhabited. The flooded streets, the broken spans, the wrecks and the mangrove taking the shore back should be what the eye finds first at every zoom, drawn for that zoom.
4. **There is no paper.** The style sheet shows ivory rag paper under ink and wash. The tiles are colour from edge to edge. Let the paper show through the washes, most of all on land, and let ink hatching carry relief and density.
5. **The city is one texture.** Downtown towers, low houses, port sheds, parks gone to jungle and beach hotels are all drawn with the same mark. Give each district its own.

## What to do

Paint it again where it falls short, with a free hand as before. Keep what is already at the bar: much of zoom 3 may only need its coasts inked and its districts told apart. Zoom 0 and zoom 1 most likely need a new approach, and zoom 2 some of each. Decide for yourself, by looking.

Before you call it finished, put the whole-map zoom beside the best illustrated maps you know of from any game or atlas and ask which one a stranger would hang on a wall. Keep going until it is this one. Say plainly in the report where it still falls short.

What must hold is unchanged: true to the data at each zoom for what that zoom draws, no seams, zooms that agree in broad colour, tiles of 1,024 pixels named as before, no lettering, border, compass or grid.

## Two practical things

- **The engine counts x the other way.** The repository now has a map file format (`planning/reference/maps.md`, `tools/map.ts`). In it, pictures are north up as the map screen shows them, places are metres from the map's south-east corner, and x grows to the west. Your layers and vectors count easting to the east from the centre. Do not build a map file yet (the format is about to gain a second version), but add to `base/VALUES.md` the exact rule from your coordinates to the engine's, checked against that document, so whoever builds the world cannot get it mirrored.
- **What is kept in the repository** is the artwork and what made it. `assets/source/maps/miami/.gitignore` now leaves out the downloads, the reference renders, the check pictures and the warped copies, since your tools make them again. Keep anything a reader needs to judge the work (measurements, the production log) in `REPORT.md` or beside it, not under `checks/`. Replace round one's tiles and originals in place; history keeps the old ones. Do not run git commands that write: the work is committed for you when the run ends.

Network access is on. The virtual environment under `tools/mapart/.venv` is still there.
# Miami — the drowned atlas, round two

The distant map has been redrawn as an illustrated atlas. **Zooms 0–2 have 21 new accepted original paintings; zoom 3 keeps its 64 original room paintings with a new paper, coast and district finish.** The delivery remains 85 north-up, 1,024 × 1,024 RGB tiles. Geography and world layers are unchanged.

[Open the whole-map painting](tiles/z0/0_0.png). [Original style sheet](style/style-sheet.png). [Production log](reports/round2-production-log.md). [Reproduction instructions](../../../../tools/mapart/README.md).

## What changed, by looking

The old overview's eleven-thousand-building mesh is gone. The bay, islands and causeways organize the picture. Downtown is a few skeletal tower groups rising out of flooded green ground; the port has roofless sheds and rust-coloured cranes; the beach has long pale hotel ruins; western neighborhoods have low courtyard shells; parks and southern shores have groves and directional grass hatching. Ivory ground shows between them. The principal roads remain geographical guides, without every local street competing with the scene or future game markers.

Zoom 1 adds district detail, still with deliberate omissions. Zoom 2 returns to the actual neighborhood fabric and has been repainted throughout: open rooms, broken warehouse bays, palms, exposed paper and more economical ground marks. Zoom 3 retains the first round's rich interiors. Warm port trusses and pale hotel galleries distinguish those footprints; downtown masonry is cooler and heavier. These district conventions are an interpretation of the future city, not an additional building-use survey.

The shoreline now has varying ink pressure, small deviations, pen lifts at beaches, a second broken stroke at urban quays, and a shallow wash that follows the source coast. It is no longer one constant dark vector stroke. The coast's underlying land/water division stays at the native data boundary; ink is permitted a narrow finishing band around it.

Flooded road corridors, four missing spans and four wrecks still come from the saved future-world layers. The overview emphasizes drowned downtown and mangrove reclamation. Wreck symbols are enlarged at z0/z1 so they survive that viewing distance; their centres and directions are exact, but their pictorial size is not a physical footprint. At z2/z3 the hull drawing uses the actual saved outline.

## Geography and scale contract

The map covers **8,128 × 8,128 m**: downtown and Brickell, the port, Biscayne Bay, the Venetian and other island chains, South Beach, Fisher Island, and northern Virginia Key. Local WGS84 Transverse Mercator is centred at 25.78° N, 80.166° W, scale 1, with bounds −4,064 to +4,064 m in easting and northing. Grid/true-north convergence is below 0.018° at the edges.

| Zoom | Native canvas | Tiles | Metres per pixel | What is drawn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 1,024² | 1 | 7.9375 | Exact coasts, islands, causeways and principal roads; generalized district wash and landmark pictures |
| 1 | 2,048² | 4 | 3.96875 | Same geographical skeleton, selected additional avenues, more ruin groups |
| 2 | 4,096² | 16 | 1.984375 | Native road corridors and building footprints, newly painted neighborhood detail |
| 3 | 8,192² | 64 | 0.9921875 | Native footprints, retained room paintings, canopy and fine shore/district treatment |

Names remain `tiles/z<zoom>/<column>_<row>.png`, with columns increasing eastward and rows southward. Every tile has no lettering, border, compass or grid. No engine map file was made.

The far geometric plans provide **32 spaced footprint anchors at z0 and 128 at z1**. These anchors direct an illustrator; they are not a claim that a generated tower's every window or projected upper storey coincides with a surveyed building. At those scales, ruins and groves are representative pictures of districts. Elevated crane arms can project over water and skyline symbols can occlude a road. Do not extract world footprints or tree positions from those pictures. At close scales, native masks clip masonry to supplied footprints; interior walls and structural bays are invented ruin drawings.

All **21 base data artifacts** checked against round one's audit have unchanged hashes; only their interpretation document, VALUES.md, changed. The base foundation is 4,065 inclusive vertex samples at 2 m spacing: 4,064 cells, or 127 chunks of 64 m. Use the canonical 8,192² masks or vectors for fine feature placement; the 2 m companions cannot preserve every narrow feature. [Integrity check](reports/base-integrity-round2.json), [original grid quantization measurements](reports/base-grid-agreement.json), [endpoint corrections](reports/canonical-layers.json).

## Engine coordinates: do not mirror this map

Checked against `planning/reference/maps.md`, `tools/map.ts` and the actual north-up layer reader in `tools/map/layers.ts`. Our `(E,N)` is east/north from the centre. The engine's `(x,z)` is west/north from the south-east corner:

```text
x = 4064 - E
z = 4064 + N
```

North-west is `(8128,8128)`, north-east `(0,8128)`, south-east `(0,0)`, south-west `(8128,0)`. **Keep the PNGs north-up; the importer already reverses the sample order.** [base/VALUES.md](base/VALUES.md) also gives inverse transforms, vertex and pixel-centre formulas, yaw conversion, reflected polygon winding and height-encoding cautions. [Corner/direction check](reports/coordinate-check.json).

## How the artwork is reproduced

Every new raster painting was made with the built-in image tool. There were **23 image calls**: 21 replacement originals, one preceding overview study retained as an art-direction input, and one preceding northeast district painting retained for its targeted correction. The correction removed erroneous port cranes from residential Belle Isle. The exact used prompts, accepted originals and these supplementary inputs are kept. The original 64 z3 paintings are unchanged. No external comparison artwork was supplied to generation.

Far views use native generalized plans and similarity registration. An early elastic correction bent architectural drawings and was rejected. Narrow displaced coast marks are cleaned before the native coast is redrawn. Close views use the established position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC registration, shoreline fallback and small local correction. Original pigment supplies penwork, rooms, plants and wash; native geometry controls material placement. A 64 px gutter gives neighboring paintings a 128 px shared blend interval.

Each zoom is assembled and finished as **one continuous canvas**. Paper, coast ink, district treatments and broad colour adjustments happen before cutting any tile. A symmetric, seven-pass RGB wash adjustment shares differences between neighboring scales without spatially moving native marks. It replaced earlier local transfer experiments that produced halos or muddy foliage. Wreck symbols are applied before the final cut as well. No special blur or edge repair is applied at tile joins.

The finishing masters, references, registration-image caches and review pictures are ignored and reconstructible. The kept originals, style sheet, base layers, prompts, code and pinned packages are sufficient. Run the current round-two sequence in [tools/mapart/README.md](../../../../tools/mapart/README.md); the old `finish.py` entry point would restore the superseded all-features-at-all-scales treatment. Its registration helpers remain in use. Image generation itself is nondeterministic; finishing from frozen originals is reproducible. Verification rebuilt both far canvases from their originals with identical hashes, recomputed three representative close registrations without their caches with zero differing pixels, and reran all four scales' colour balance and export: all 85 final tile hashes were identical.

## Measurements and their limits

The format audit passes: **85 RGB 1,024² tiles, 85 accepted originals, corresponding prompts, correct grayscale base sizes and bit depths**. Each tile set reconstructs its uncut canvas with **zero differing RGB values**.

| Parent comparison | Raw mean absolute RGB difference /255 | 8 px blurred mean difference /255 | Mean RGB shift /255 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| z1 → z0 | 13.645 | **0.802** | +0.492, +0.519, +0.530 |
| z2 → z1 | 15.738 | **1.440** | +0.662, +0.578, +0.645 |
| z3 → z2 | 11.622 | **1.028** | +0.480, +0.500, +0.516 |

All three broad-colour comparisons remain below 2/255. Raw differences are larger because a far landmark picture and a close floorplan are intentionally different drawings. The test reduces the child by a 2× box filter and compares exported RGB, with an 8 px Gaussian comparison separating broad pigment from native detail.

All **140 tile-edge segments** were measured independently: 4 at z1, 24 at z2, 112 at z3. The mean absolute RGB jump across each join is compared with the other boundaries in a 66-boundary neighborhood.

| Zoom | Join-ratio minimum | Join-ratio maximum | Reconstruction error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| z0 | — | — | 0 |
| z1 | 0.956 | 1.118 | 0 |
| z2 | 0.643 | 1.568 | 0 |
| z3 | 0.458 | 1.401 | 0 |

**The raw worst ratio is higher than round one's independently reported 1.29; that numerical bound is not claimed here.** The largest value is at z2, horizontal y=1024, segment x=1024…2047. A real building wall lies across the first 44 pixels of that cut: its jump is 39.88 versus 12.31 beside it. In the large open-water portion, x=1152…2047, the join jump is 1.47 and the adjacent jumps average about 1.51. Inspection of the largest ratios, native joined strips and complete contact sheets shows continuous painting, not a tile-shaped colour or drawing discontinuity. Softening every wall to improve that statistic was tested and rejected. The complete unselected set of ratios is retained, not just favourable examples.

The independent teal-pigment diagnostic puts **99.38–99.61% of sampled source shoreline pixels within 2 pixels** of a visible teal edge. Its maximum distances are 5.10, 17.03, 19.00 and 19.03 pixels by zoom. Inspection locates the largest outliers at crane symbols, dark thin causeway decks, quays and grey/green water: a palette classifier cannot distinguish every ink or flood mark from coastline. These numbers are **one-way pigment proximity, not full coast IoU and not a certificate of surveying accuracy**. The coast ink's mathematical wavering is at most 0.66 pixel; thickening/double strokes occupy a wider narrow band. Exact selected-road support matches the source-rendered corridors at every zoom, before pictorial occlusion. Neither support identity nor a pigment score proves the correctness of every illustrative detail.

Evidence is kept outside ignored `checks/`: [all exported measurements](reports/round2-measurements.json), [delivery audit](reports/round2-delivery-audit.json), [tile/original/base hashes](reports/round2-sha256.json), [colour adjustment](reports/round2-balance.json), [shore diagnostic locations](reports/coast-diagnostic-locations.json), [registration reproduction](reports/round2-registration-reproduction.json), [export reproduction](reports/round2-reproduction.json). The old measurements remain explicitly labelled [round one](reports/round1-measurements.json).

## The wall test, and where this still falls short

I put the whole-map image beside **Caroline Harper's [Sea of Thieves commission](https://www.carolineharper.com/portfolio-2/sea-of-thieves)**, **Joan Blaeu's [Amsterdam, 1649](https://www.mapsperhaps.com/products/amstelodami-celeberrimi-hollandiae-emporii-delineatio-nova-1)**, and **Pauline Baynes's [Middle-earth map, reproduced by the Library of Congress](https://blogs.loc.gov/loc/2016/10/lcm-mapping-the-imaginary/)**. They were comparisons for visual criticism only; their lettering, borders, figures and decorative devices were not imported into the tiles.

For this brief, **I would frame this Miami overview**. The open teal bay gives the skeletal skyline, diagonal port and pale beach a clear composition at viewing distance. The change from a tiny street plan to a few purposeful pictures is decisive. The paper and quiet water also leave room for the game's coloured cells. This is an artistic judgment, not evidence that every stranger would prefer it to those maps.

It still falls short of those illustrators in the individuality of every small mark. Some palms and courtyard ruins repeat a common vocabulary; Baynes has more local surprises and Harper more varied miniature narratives. The close views remain more geometric than a wholly freehand atlas because actual footprints are enforced. Large quays and straight causeways still reveal their engineered geometry. The real missing spans are small at overview scale; drowned ground and skeletal towers carry more of the first glance than those breaks. Broad colour continuity cannot make a miniature tower turn continuously into a top-down room plan: the zoom change deliberately changes the cartographic convention. Those are visible limits, not claims concealed by a successful numerical audit.

## Sources and world-building limits

[SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) retains attribution and licences; [downloads.json](downloads.json) retains exact requests and source hashes. Geography was not reacquired or changed in this round:

- NOAA 2021 Miami-Dade bare-earth DEM, 369 intersecting tiles, CC0. Surveyed coverage is 99.9714% of source land samples; 2,203 land samples are absent. Heights −5.53 to 17.18 m NAVD88, converted from US survey feet.
- Census TIGER/Line 2025: 38 clipped water polygons and 1,184 road features. Shorelines are cartographic, not cadastral; road corridor widths are authored around source centrelines.
- FEMA/ORNL USA Structures: 11,919 clipped footprints. The delivery item declares CC BY 4.0; retain the conservative attribution in SOURCES.md when redistributing.
- USGS NLCD 2021: land-cover classes at their actual approximately 30 m source resolution.

Reclamation, mangrove, low-street flooding, bridge gaps, wrecks and the frozen painted canopy describe an invented future. Room walls, crane shapes, tower heights and hotel/gallery treatments are illustrative. Source dates differ; FEMA can omit smaller structures. No bathymetry was acquired. Missing height values use an explicit −1 m convention with a separate validity mask; shallow colour does not encode measured depth. This is artwork and shared geographic data, not a finished 3D world or an engine map file.

# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style

An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.

## Pigment anchors

| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |

## Symbols and scale

Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.

Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.

Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

## Round two: scale and paper take priority

The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:

- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. A small pictorial skyline, port sheds/cranes, courtyard ruins and beach hotels are representative district symbols. Their projected heights are illustrative; do not read a symbol's drawn silhouette as a surveyed building footprint.
- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.

`paper-study.png` is the first round-two art direction study, retained because it was an input to the accepted overview. Its geometry is not authoritative. Its elastic finishing experiment was rejected for warping architecture. The production log records the subsequent corrections.
# Miami map-art tools

Offline source/art tools only. They add no dependency to the engine or its build.

## Current delivery: round two

The original geographic pipeline below remains authoritative for source layers. The current art finish is **round2.py**, followed by **round2_balance.py**. Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.

Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
```

Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. `round2_restore.py` reconstructs these for z2/z3 without altering the historical used prompts; run it immediately after `reference.py`, as above. Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals. The context-generation tools listed below are for commissioning new paintings and can overwrite prompts; they are not part of the reproduction sequence.

| Round-two tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.

The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

## Original geographic preparation and round-one tools

From the repository root, create the isolated environment:

```sh
python3 -m venv tools/mapart/.venv
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/pip install -r tools/mapart/requirements.txt
```

The frozen bounds, projection and sample conventions are in `assets/source/maps/miami/map.json`. Python 3.9 was used; exact package versions are pinned. Raw data and the virtual environment are ignored by git.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| fetch.py | Download intersecting NOAA DEM tiles, county TIGER ZIPs, NLCD coverage and paginated FEMA footprints. Write exact request URLs and SHA-256 checksums to downloads.json. Reuses existing downloads. |
| prepare.py | Clip/reproject vectors, reproject bare-earth height, rasterize 4,065 vertex samples, preserve NLCD codes, author explicit succession and low-street flooding. Checks FEMA pages against the complete object-ID inventory. |
| future.py | Freeze four missing bridge spans and four submerged wrecks as shared world geometry; mark tunnels as subterranean. Run after prepare.py. |
| reference.py [zooms...] | Render geographic references afresh from the vector data at each native zoom, with water/road/building masks. Default: all four zooms. |
| contexts.py Z | Build each tile's 64 px neighboring overlap, parent-paint context, exact prompt and queue.json for the built-in image tool. |
| finish.py Z | Similarity registration, local shoreline registration, class-constrained pigment and architectural detail, overlapping assembly, parent-color matching, exact cutting into 1,024 px PNGs. Requires every original painting for that zoom. |
| finish.py Z --partial | Pilot only: export already-painted tiles while keeping explicitly provisional parent proxies under checks/partial_zZ.png. Never use partial images as a completed delivery. |
| alignment.py | Position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC registration of original ink against geographic corners, with multistart main-water-silhouette similarity fitting for sparse scenes. Used by finish.py; cache metadata retains fit residuals and transforms. |
| preregister.py Z --watch | Populate registration caches as originals arrive. Stops when that zoom is complete; does not export tiles. |
| author_canopy.py | Freeze vegetation crowns from the complete registered zoom-3 painting as shared fictional world layers. Run once, then finish zooms 0 through 3 in order. |
| canonical.py | Save 8,192 px canonical water/road/building masks; repair classifications at inclusive outer grid samples and preserve surface roads over tunnels. Run after native references. |
| measure.py | Independently classify visible features from exported RGB; measure IoU, symmetric boundary distances, exact tile reconstruction, seam jumps, and parent-scale color differences. |
| grid_check.py | Quantify the difference between the engine's 2 m vertex samples and the finest native vector masks, independently of artwork. |
| review.py Z reference/raw/final [--row R] | Labeled contact sheets for review, under checks; never adds labels to game tiles. |
| audit.py | Assert tile count, RGB format, original-paint presence, base dimensions and bit depth; hash delivery artifacts. |

Build sources and references:


Image generation is an explicit art-production step using the **built-in image tool**, not an API-key script. The overview prompt is under paintings/z0; later queues are made by contexts.py. Each queue entry lists its geometry reference, accepted parent, original style sheet and output filename. Inspect inputs, issue the prompt with those local references, then copy the returned original PNG to `paintings/zZ/C_R.raw.png`. Preserve supplementary prompt files. Do not resize or overwrite the raw originals. The tool returned 1,254 px squares during this run. The finishing code maps each to its 1,152 px overlap region (or 1,024 px overview).

After a complete zoom is painted:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/finish.py 1
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/contexts.py 2
```

Review the full map, representative full-resolution tiles, and joined boundaries. Exact geometry measurements do not establish artistic quality. Never accept solely on an RGB-mask score.

The offline viewer is `assets/source/maps/miami/checks/viewer.html`; open it directly in a browser. It reads the actual PNG tiles, supports pan/zoom and a fixed-camera painting comparison, and draws optional diagnostic overlays independently. No server or dependencies are required.

# Miami — the drowned atlas, round two

The distant map has been redrawn as an illustrated atlas. **Zooms 0–2 have 21 new accepted original paintings; zoom 3 keeps its 64 original room paintings with a new paper, coast and district finish.** The delivery remains 85 north-up, 1,024 × 1,024 RGB tiles. Geography and world layers are unchanged.

[Open the whole-map painting](tiles/z0/0_0.png). [Original style sheet](style/style-sheet.png). [Production log](reports/round2-production-log.md). [Reproduction instructions](../../../../tools/mapart/README.md).

## What changed, by looking

The old overview's eleven-thousand-building mesh is gone. The bay, islands and causeways organize the picture. Downtown is a few skeletal tower groups rising out of flooded green ground; the port has roofless sheds and rust-coloured cranes; the beach has long pale hotel ruins; western neighborhoods have low courtyard shells; parks and southern shores have groves and directional grass hatching. Ivory ground shows between them. The principal roads remain geographical guides, without every local street competing with the scene or future game markers.

Zoom 1 adds district detail, still with deliberate omissions. Zoom 2 returns to the actual neighborhood fabric and has been repainted throughout: open rooms, broken warehouse bays, palms, exposed paper and more economical ground marks. Zoom 3 retains the first round's rich interiors. Warm port trusses and pale hotel galleries distinguish those footprints; downtown masonry is cooler and heavier. These district conventions are an interpretation of the future city, not an additional building-use survey.

The shoreline now has varying ink pressure, small deviations, pen lifts at beaches, a second broken stroke at urban quays, and a shallow wash that follows the source coast. It is no longer one constant dark vector stroke. The coast's underlying land/water division stays at the native data boundary; ink is permitted a narrow finishing band around it.

Flooded road corridors, four missing spans and four wrecks still come from the saved future-world layers. The overview emphasizes drowned downtown and mangrove reclamation. Wreck symbols are enlarged at z0/z1 so they survive that viewing distance; their centres and directions are exact, but their pictorial size is not a physical footprint. At z2/z3 the hull drawing uses the actual saved outline.

## Geography and scale contract

The map covers **8,128 × 8,128 m**: downtown and Brickell, the port, Biscayne Bay, the Venetian and other island chains, South Beach, Fisher Island, and northern Virginia Key. Local WGS84 Transverse Mercator is centred at 25.78° N, 80.166° W, scale 1, with bounds −4,064 to +4,064 m in easting and northing. Grid/true-north convergence is below 0.018° at the edges.

| Zoom | Native canvas | Tiles | Metres per pixel | What is drawn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 1,024² | 1 | 7.9375 | Exact coasts, islands, causeways and principal roads; generalized district wash and landmark pictures |
| 1 | 2,048² | 4 | 3.96875 | Same geographical skeleton, selected additional avenues, more ruin groups |
| 2 | 4,096² | 16 | 1.984375 | Native road corridors and building footprints, newly painted neighborhood detail |
| 3 | 8,192² | 64 | 0.9921875 | Native footprints, retained room paintings, canopy and fine shore/district treatment |

Names remain `tiles/z<zoom>/<column>_<row>.png`, with columns increasing eastward and rows southward. Every tile has no lettering, border, compass or grid. No engine map file was made.

The far geometric plans provide **32 spaced footprint anchors at z0 and 128 at z1**. These anchors direct an illustrator; they are not a claim that a generated tower's every window or projected upper storey coincides with a surveyed building. At those scales, ruins and groves are representative pictures of districts. Elevated crane arms can project over water and skyline symbols can occlude a road. Do not extract world footprints or tree positions from those pictures. At close scales, native masks clip masonry to supplied footprints; interior walls and structural bays are invented ruin drawings.

All **21 base data artifacts** checked against round one's audit have unchanged hashes; only their interpretation document, VALUES.md, changed. The base foundation is 4,065 inclusive vertex samples at 2 m spacing: 4,064 cells, or 127 chunks of 64 m. Use the canonical 8,192² masks or vectors for fine feature placement; the 2 m companions cannot preserve every narrow feature. [Integrity check](reports/base-integrity-round2.json), [original grid quantization measurements](reports/base-grid-agreement.json), [endpoint corrections](reports/canonical-layers.json).

## Engine coordinates: do not mirror this map

Checked against `planning/reference/maps.md`, `tools/map.ts` and the actual north-up layer reader in `tools/map/layers.ts`. Our `(E,N)` is east/north from the centre. The engine's `(x,z)` is west/north from the south-east corner:

```text
x = 4064 - E
z = 4064 + N
```

North-west is `(8128,8128)`, north-east `(0,8128)`, south-east `(0,0)`, south-west `(8128,0)`. **Keep the PNGs north-up; the importer already reverses the sample order.** [base/VALUES.md](base/VALUES.md) also gives inverse transforms, vertex and pixel-centre formulas, yaw conversion, reflected polygon winding and height-encoding cautions. [Corner/direction check](reports/coordinate-check.json).

## How the artwork is reproduced

Every new raster painting was made with the built-in image tool. There were **23 image calls**: 21 replacement originals, one preceding overview study retained as an art-direction input, and one preceding northeast district painting retained for its targeted correction. The correction removed erroneous port cranes from residential Belle Isle. The exact used prompts, accepted originals and these supplementary inputs are kept. The original 64 z3 paintings are unchanged. No external comparison artwork was supplied to generation.

Far views use native generalized plans and similarity registration. An early elastic correction bent architectural drawings and was rejected. Narrow displaced coast marks are cleaned before the native coast is redrawn. Close views use the established position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC registration, shoreline fallback and small local correction. Original pigment supplies penwork, rooms, plants and wash; native geometry controls material placement. A 64 px gutter gives neighboring paintings a 128 px shared blend interval.

Each zoom is assembled and finished as **one continuous canvas**. Paper, coast ink, district treatments and broad colour adjustments happen before cutting any tile. A symmetric, seven-pass RGB wash adjustment shares differences between neighboring scales without spatially moving native marks. It replaced earlier local transfer experiments that produced halos or muddy foliage. Wreck symbols are applied before the final cut as well. No special blur or edge repair is applied at tile joins.

The finishing masters, references, registration-image caches and review pictures are ignored and reconstructible. The kept originals, style sheet, base layers, prompts, code and pinned packages are sufficient. Run the current round-two sequence in [tools/mapart/README.md](../../../../tools/mapart/README.md); the old `finish.py` entry point would restore the superseded all-features-at-all-scales treatment. Its registration helpers remain in use. Image generation itself is nondeterministic; finishing from frozen originals is reproducible. Verification rebuilt both far canvases from their originals with identical hashes, recomputed three representative close registrations without their caches with zero differing pixels, and reran all four scales' colour balance and export: all 85 final tile hashes were identical.

## Measurements and their limits

The format audit passes: **85 RGB 1,024² tiles, 85 accepted originals, corresponding prompts, correct grayscale base sizes and bit depths**. Each tile set reconstructs its uncut canvas with **zero differing RGB values**.

| Parent comparison | Raw mean absolute RGB difference /255 | 8 px blurred mean difference /255 | Mean RGB shift /255 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| z1 → z0 | 13.645 | **0.802** | +0.492, +0.519, +0.530 |
| z2 → z1 | 15.738 | **1.440** | +0.662, +0.578, +0.645 |
| z3 → z2 | 11.622 | **1.028** | +0.480, +0.500, +0.516 |

All three broad-colour comparisons remain below 2/255. Raw differences are larger because a far landmark picture and a close floorplan are intentionally different drawings. The test reduces the child by a 2× box filter and compares exported RGB, with an 8 px Gaussian comparison separating broad pigment from native detail.

All **140 tile-edge segments** were measured independently: 4 at z1, 24 at z2, 112 at z3. The mean absolute RGB jump across each join is compared with the other boundaries in a 66-boundary neighborhood.

| Zoom | Join-ratio minimum | Join-ratio maximum | Reconstruction error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| z0 | — | — | 0 |
| z1 | 0.956 | 1.118 | 0 |
| z2 | 0.643 | 1.568 | 0 |
| z3 | 0.458 | 1.401 | 0 |

**The raw worst ratio is higher than round one's independently reported 1.29; that numerical bound is not claimed here.** The largest value is at z2, horizontal y=1024, segment x=1024…2047. A real building wall lies across the first 44 pixels of that cut: its jump is 39.88 versus 12.31 beside it. In the large open-water portion, x=1152…2047, the join jump is 1.47 and the adjacent jumps average about 1.51. Inspection of the largest ratios, native joined strips and complete contact sheets shows continuous painting, not a tile-shaped colour or drawing discontinuity. Softening every wall to improve that statistic was tested and rejected. The complete unselected set of ratios is retained, not just favourable examples.

The independent teal-pigment diagnostic puts **99.38–99.61% of sampled source shoreline pixels within 2 pixels** of a visible teal edge. Its maximum distances are 5.10, 17.03, 19.00 and 19.03 pixels by zoom. Inspection locates the largest outliers at crane symbols, dark thin causeway decks, quays and grey/green water: a palette classifier cannot distinguish every ink or flood mark from coastline. These numbers are **one-way pigment proximity, not full coast IoU and not a certificate of surveying accuracy**. The coast ink's mathematical wavering is at most 0.66 pixel; thickening/double strokes occupy a wider narrow band. Exact selected-road support matches the source-rendered corridors at every zoom, before pictorial occlusion. Neither support identity nor a pigment score proves the correctness of every illustrative detail.

Evidence is kept outside ignored `checks/`: [all exported measurements](reports/round2-measurements.json), [delivery audit](reports/round2-delivery-audit.json), [tile/original/base hashes](reports/round2-sha256.json), [colour adjustment](reports/round2-balance.json), [shore diagnostic locations](reports/coast-diagnostic-locations.json), [registration reproduction](reports/round2-registration-reproduction.json), [export reproduction](reports/round2-reproduction.json). The old measurements remain explicitly labelled [round one](reports/round1-measurements.json).

## The wall test, and where this still falls short

I put the whole-map image beside **Caroline Harper's [Sea of Thieves commission](https://www.carolineharper.com/portfolio-2/sea-of-thieves)**, **Joan Blaeu's [Amsterdam, 1649](https://www.mapsperhaps.com/products/amstelodami-celeberrimi-hollandiae-emporii-delineatio-nova-1)**, and **Pauline Baynes's [Middle-earth map, reproduced by the Library of Congress](https://blogs.loc.gov/loc/2016/10/lcm-mapping-the-imaginary/)**. They were comparisons for visual criticism only; their lettering, borders, figures and decorative devices were not imported into the tiles.

For this brief, **I would frame this Miami overview**. The open teal bay gives the skeletal skyline, diagonal port and pale beach a clear composition at viewing distance. The change from a tiny street plan to a few purposeful pictures is decisive. The paper and quiet water also leave room for the game's coloured cells. This is an artistic judgment, not evidence that every stranger would prefer it to those maps.

It still falls short of those illustrators in the individuality of every small mark. Some palms and courtyard ruins repeat a common vocabulary; Baynes has more local surprises and Harper more varied miniature narratives. The close views remain more geometric than a wholly freehand atlas because actual footprints are enforced. Large quays and straight causeways still reveal their engineered geometry. The real missing spans are small at overview scale; drowned ground and skeletal towers carry more of the first glance than those breaks. Broad colour continuity cannot make a miniature tower turn continuously into a top-down room plan: the zoom change deliberately changes the cartographic convention. Those are visible limits, not claims concealed by a successful numerical audit.

## Sources and world-building limits

[SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) retains attribution and licences; [downloads.json](downloads.json) retains exact requests and source hashes. Geography was not reacquired or changed in this round:

- NOAA 2021 Miami-Dade bare-earth DEM, 369 intersecting tiles, CC0. Surveyed coverage is 99.9714% of source land samples; 2,203 land samples are absent. Heights −5.53 to 17.18 m NAVD88, converted from US survey feet.
- Census TIGER/Line 2025: 38 clipped water polygons and 1,184 road features. Shorelines are cartographic, not cadastral; road corridor widths are authored around source centrelines.
- FEMA/ORNL USA Structures: 11,919 clipped footprints. The delivery item declares CC BY 4.0; retain the conservative attribution in SOURCES.md when redistributing.
- USGS NLCD 2021: land-cover classes at their actual approximately 30 m source resolution.

Reclamation, mangrove, low-street flooding, bridge gaps, wrecks and the frozen painted canopy describe an invented future. Room walls, crane shapes, tower heights and hotel/gallery treatments are illustrative. Source dates differ; FEMA can omit smaller structures. No bathymetry was acquired. Missing height values use an explicit −1 m convention with a separate validity mask; shallow colour does not encode measured depth. This is artwork and shared geographic data, not a finished 3D world or an engine map file.
